entities.summary:
Muvaffak (muvaffak) was a 10th-century Persian physician who made significant contributions to the field of medicine, particularly in the area of pharmacology. Born in unknown, Muwaffaq Harawī died in 976 CE and is considered one of the most important figures in Persian medical history. His work, including the book "Kitab al-Shihab al-Maksuy" (The Book of the Shining Star), had a lasting impact on the development of Arabic and Islamic medicine.

  Muwaffaq's work built upon the discoveries of earlier physicians, such as Avicenna, and introduced new treatments and remedies that were used for centuries. His influence can still be seen in modern medicine, particularly in the use of herbal remedies and traditional Persian medicine.

  Muwaffaq's legacy extends beyond his medical contributions, as he played a key role in promoting the spread of knowledge and learning throughout the Islamic world. His work was widely disseminated and studied by scholars across the Middle East and Europe, making him one of the most important figures in the transmission of knowledge during the Islamic Golden Age.
